newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end up as supply and demand balance seen tight.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end up as supply and demand balance seen tight.

text.p: Key December Japanese government bond futures ended slightly higher on Tuesday after healthy demand appeared for the twenty-year JGBs offered through an auction.
"There wasn't any reason to sell today. The twenty-year JGB auction went pretty well and this helped to push JGBs up," said a trust bank trader.
There was some buying right after Japan's August machinery orders data was released on Tuesday, which came in worse than expected, but that later tapered off, traders said.
The December closed at 123.15, up slightly from Monday's 123.05.
The key futures contract moved in a range of 122.92 to 123.30 during the day.
Machinery orders fell a seasonally adjusted 11.1 percent in August from the previous month to 1.05 trillion yen, the Economic Planning Agency said on Tuesday.
"Machinery orders came in weaker than expected and this should be a factor to buy, but they (JGBs) were sold afterwards instead," the trust bank trader said.

Traders might have been reluctant to buy based solely on the machinery orders data, since they had not yet seen the results of the twenty-year JGB auction which were due later in the afternoon, a trader for another trust bank said.
The Ministry of Finance said on Tuesday that the auction of 400 billion yen worth of 3.5 percent twenty-year JGBs produced a lowest price of 100.50 and an average price of 100.55.
In the morning, cash JGBs as well as the key futures contract rose, helped by the Bank of Japan's outright bond buying operation worth 200 billion yen, traders said.
"Under the new rolling settlement system...it has become harder to predict when outright bond buying operations will take place," the second trader said.
This means the market is more likely to rise after outright bond buying operations than before, since the market has more difficulty absorbing the effects of the operation beforehand, he said.
Market sentiment was also bullish in the morning on talk that a fund being set up to wind up failed mortgage companies will receive 907 billion yen worth of cash on October 17, traders said.
The cash will basically be available for bond investment, they said.
The yield of the benchmark 182nd cash JGB stood at 2.745 percent as of 0719 GMT, down from Monday's 2.75 percent.
